title: GPU eviction surge capture + handoff quickstart
content:
Purpose:
This document is a compact triage and evidence-capture playbook for short-lived GPU eviction surges that cause brownouts in hosting pools. It's intentionally concise so a nightshift engineer can capture the right signals, take safe mitigations, and hand off a high-quality packet to SRE owners for deeper analysis.

Context / why this exists:
- We observed several multi-node, short-window eviction spikes over the last 8 weeks where nodes showed bursts of correctable ECC, then either NVLink retrains or kernel-level driver hang -> eviction.
- Past tickets dug into single-failure modes; we lack a lightweight checklist that focuses on capturing transient signals (pre-eviction telemetry, nvlink negotiation logs, driver OOPS) and safe automated containment.

Quick incident summary template (fill this out first on call):
- window_start: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM UTC
- affected_pool: (e.g., prod-a100-pool-3)
- affected_nodes_count: N
- observed_symptoms: (e.g., correctable ECC burst, dmesg: NVRM: X, NVLink retrain logs)
- initial_action_taken: (evicted nodes/drained, restarted driver, quarantined)
- handoff_to: Name + pager/team

Minimum evidence to capture (high priority — short window):
1) Telemetry snapshot (must snapshot, not just rely on long-term TS):
   - gpu-counters: run `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,POWER,MEMORY,PERF -i <id>` for each affected GPU; save output to /tmp/evict-YYYYMMDD-HHMM.txt
   - driver logs: `dmesg --ctime | tail -n 200` and `journalctl -u nvidia-driver.service -n 200` (or equivalent) -> save
   - nvlink: `nvidia-smi nvlink --status` (older drivers: `nvidia-smi topo -m` + `nvidia-smi -q --display=NVLINK`)
   - kernel oopses: `sudo cat /var/log/kern.log | grep -i -E "NVRM|gpu|nvlink|kernel panic" -n`
   - pod/container state snapshots: `kubectl get pods -n <ns> -o wide --field-selector=spec.nodeName=<node>` and `kubectl describe pod <pod>` for example crashed pods
   - perf counters: if configured, pull metrics from /metrics endpoint for the affected node id

2) Telemetry retention note:
   - When surges are brief, telemetry streams often get sampled out. If you can, increase sampling window temporarily (sre-admin-run) or trigger a high-fidelity grab from the collector: `curl -X POST http://telemetry-snap.internal/snapshot?n=60&node=<node>` (internal API). Notify telemetry on-call if snapshot fails.

Short triage decision tree (first 15 minutes):
- If kernel panic / driver OOPS present: quarantine node from scheduler, collect /var/crash, and escalate to eng-serving-runtime immediately.
- If only correctable ECC spikes (no panics) but sustained across >2 GPUs on same host: mark node as noisy and schedule eviction to safe pool; set hardware quarantine label for follow-up.
- If NVLink negotiation flaps (retrain logs in dmesg, link down/up sequences): isolate node (drain) and attempt to repro in lab with identical BIOS/firmware versions. Do not hot-reboot repeatedly.

Safe mitigations (minimal risk, reversible):
1) Drain the node from scheduler: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (only if eviction impact acceptable).
2) Add node to a temporary quarantine pool tag for automated scheduler avoidance.
3) If driver process hung but kernel alive: try `sudo systemctl restart nvidia-driver` or `modprobe -r nvidia && modprobe nvidia` -> only with approval from SRE lead during high-QPS windows.
4) Do NOT: power-cycle racks unless directed by datacenter ops. Reboots can obscure pre-failure signals.

Evidence preservation checklist (critical for root cause):
- copy all captured files to the incident bucket: `gsutil cp /tmp/evict-* gs://redwood-incident-evidence/<incidentid>/`
- attach pod yaml and node description to ticket
- record exact git commit and driver package versions: `dpkg -l | grep nvidia` or `rpm -qa | grep nvidia` and kernel version `uname -a`
- take a photo of the node sticker if investigating pre-deployment hardware changes (rare but useful when firmware mismatches suspected)

Hypotheses to consider (quick mapping to where to look):
- ECC burst -> memory module marginal stability or power transient; check BMC logs and power delivery telemetry
- NVLink retrain loop -> link negotiation hardware/firmware or race in driver stack; check nvlink link counters and bios/firmware inventory
- Driver hang/kernel panic after ECC -> driver exposure to repeated correctable errors triggering unrecoverable state; cross-check driver version test matrix
- Localized thermal anomalies -> correlate with temperature telemetry and cooling events

When to escalate (samples):
- >5% of a pool evicted in <30 minutes -> P1 (impacting throughput SLO)
- single node producing repeated panics across 3+ reboots -> escalate to hardware/ops (possible bad board)
- driver OOPS with stack trace referencing `nvlink` or `nv_rdma` -> page serving-runtime on-call

Runbook additions recommended (for PR after postmortem):
- automated short-window telemetry grab triggered by eviction spike with retention TTL 7 days
- eviction-safety label automation: when node exhibits >X correctable ECC/min for Y minutes, mark for auto-drain + quarantine
- expanded driver upgrade matrix testing for recent kernel versions and NVLink-heavy topologies
- new probes: NVLink link-count monotonic counters, ECC per-page heatmap aggregation

Lab repro experiments (owner + plan):
- experiment-1: reproduce NVLink retrain by toggling link speed via BIOS and inducing synthetic cross-GPU traffic (owner Lena Patel; ETA 2 weeks)
- experiment-2: inject correctable ECC patterns using memtest harness across different voltage rails to check sensitivity (owner Omar Ruiz; ETA 3 weeks, coordinate with HW ops)

Handoff notes for nightshift -> day SRE (one-line status + artifacts):
- handoff-title: `evict-surge-<incidentid> - short window noisy nodes`
- immediate-state: (drained/quarantined/normal)
- artifacts-uploaded: yes/no + GCS path
- followups: (list) e.g., contact telemetry to retrieve packet capture, schedule hardware inspection for node <id>

Post-incident analysis prompts (for the follow-up writeup):
- timeline alignment: map telemetry wall clock to node time; check for clock drift
- correlate BMC/System logs with ECC bursts (power or DIMM resets around the same timestamp)
- cross-check kernel oops against driver release notes for known NVLink regressions
- quantify cost: estimate lost tokens and customer incident impact for SLA reporting

Quick references / commands (copyable):
- `nvidia-smi -q -d ECC,HEALTH -i 0 > /tmp/evict-$(date +%s)-gpu0.txt`
- `dmesg -T | grep -i -E "NVRM|nvlink|ecc|GPU" | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg-evict.txt`
- `sudo journalctl -k -u systemd -S "-1h" | grep -i nvrm > /tmp/journal-nvrm.txt`
- `kubectl get nodes -l pool=<pool> -o wide` and `kubectl cordon <node>`

Owners and immediate contacts:
- oncall SRE: night-sre duty roster (pager as usual)
- engineering escalation: eng-serving-runtime on-call (pager)
- telemetry: telemetry-oncall@gmail.internal (DM in Slack #sre-telemetry)

Open questions to close in postmortem:
- Are we seeing a firmware skew across this fleet segment? (inventory check)
- Does our sampling rate mask short-lived NVLink flaps? (tuning needed)
- Is automatic quarantine threshold set too low/high? (adjust via experimentation)

Notes and caveats:
- This quickstart favors evidence preservation over immediate hardware resets. The most useful follow-ups come from preserved pre-eviction state.
- Document is intentionally terse; expand into a full runbook after a confirmed postmortem.

Last updated notes:
- 2029-12-02: initial sketch by Maya Chen during midnight triage
- 2029-12-08: added telemetry snapshot API and safe mitigations (Lena)
- 2029-12-15: final checklist additions and lab experiment owners (Omar)

END
